questions.title: Largest Mural on Stone Slabs (Largest Rectangle in Histogram)
questions.statement:
Imagine a wall made of $n$ vertical stone slabs placed side by side. Each slab has a width of 1 unit, but their heights are different.

You want to paint the largest possible rectangular mural (artwork) on this wall. What is the maximum area of the mural that can be painted on the slabs?
questions.input_format: integer `n` — the number of stone slabs; array.integer64 `heights` — the heights of each stone slab.
questions.output_format: integer64 — the maximum area of the wall mural.
questions.constraints:
$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$
$1 \le heights[i] \le 10^9$
Execution time limit: 0.5 s (C++), 3 s (Java), 4 s (Python 3); memory limit 1 GB.
questions.function_signature: C++: long long solution(int n, vector<long long> heights)

examples.explanation: Heights 5,3,3,2,4 (indices 2..6) with min height 2 give area 2*5 = 10.

questions.explanation: For each bar find the nearest smaller bar to the left and right with a monotonic increasing stack; area = h[i] * (right - left - 1). Take the max using 64-bit arithmetic (up to 2e5 * 1e9). O(n) time, O(n) space.

questions.pattern: minimum window containing all required items
questions.title: Smallest Sub-chain Containing All Golden Elements
questions.statement:
As space explorers, we research different soil samples and extract a chain of elements from them. There is a specific set of elements known as **Golden Elements**.

Write a function that finds the smallest sub-chain (contiguous) that includes all the golden elements. If no such sub-chain exists containing all the golden elements, return an empty sub-chain.
questions.input_format: array.string `chain` — chain of elements we search in; array.string `elements` — elements we want to find (elements in this array are unique).
questions.output_format: array.string — the smallest chain that has all the `elements` inside.
questions.constraints:
$0 < chain.length < 10^6$
$0 < elements.length < 10^3$
Elements in `elements` are unique.
Execution time limit: 1 s (C++), 4 s (Python 3); memory limit 1 GB.
questions.function_signature: C++: vector<string> solution(vector<string> chain, vector<string> elements); Python: def solution(chain, elements)

examples.explanation: The smallest sub-chain containing both "Li" and "C".

questions.explanation: Classic minimum window: map each golden element to a counter; expand right pointer, track how many distinct golden elements are covered; when all covered, shrink left while still valid and record the best window. Return the slice (empty if none). O(|chain|) time with hashing, O(|elements|) space.

questions.title: Rhombic Cipher
questions.statement:
*Rhombic Cipher* is an ingenious cipher that is used to encrypt rectangular tables of characters of size $2n \times n$. The encryption process can be described as follows:

- First create a rhombus out of the table's rows, considering them one by one from top to bottom:
  - each row is written diagonally and goes from bottom to top and from left to right;
  - the $i^{th}$ row begins at the $(i \text{ div } 2)^{th}$ line of the rhombus, counting from bottom to top (where `div` means integer division);
  - each symbol of the row is written to the left of the symbols already present at that rhombus line.
- Then the diagonals of the rhombus that go from bottom to top and from right to left are written down, which produces a new $2n \times n$ table.

Your task is to encrypt the given `table` with Rhombic Cipher.

Example encryption process (rows → rhombus lines → output rows):
```
abc        ro         djp
def        qnli       agm
ghi   ->   pmkhfc ->  ekq
jkl        jgeb       bhn
mno        da         flr
pqr                   cio
```
(The rhombus is shown top line first; `da` is line 0 at the bottom.)
questions.input_format: array.array.char `table` — a matrix of size $2n \times n$ for some integer $n \ge 0$, each element of which is a lowercase English letter.
questions.constraints:
$0 \le table.length \le 20$
$1 \le table[0].length \le 10$
Execution time limit: 0.5 s (C++); memory limit 1 GB.

examples.explanation: Rhombus lines bottom to top: "da", "jgeb", "pmkhfc", "qnli", "ro". Reading the diagonals bottom-to-top, right-to-left gives djp, agm, ekq, bhn, flr, cio.

questions.explanation: Build the rhombus as a list of 2n-1 lines (deques): for row i and column j, push table[i][j] to the front of line (i div 2) + j. Then assign coordinates to each line (line L is centered, characters at alternating positions) and read off the anti-diagonals in the required order to fill the 2n x n output row by row. Pure simulation, O(n^2).

questions.pattern: state-space search on small grid (Tetris-like block drops)
questions.title: Fill the First Column with Thrown Blocks (Min and Max Moves)
questions.statement:
You are given a rectangular board divided into a uniform grid (square cells). Some cells of the board are occupied with blocks, and others are empty. You are trying to add more and more blocks to the board, and your task is to fill the first column with them.

You can add a block to the field in the following way: first, you choose the row index, then you throw the new block into the chosen row from the left. The block appears in the leftmost cell of the row and starts moving to the right, until it reaches another block or the end of the row. When that happens, the block starts falling down until it reaches another block or the last row.

For example, if the board looks like this
```
...#..
...#..
.#....
```
(blocks are denoted by `'#'` and empty cells by `'.'`) and you throw a block into the first or the second row from the top, it will end up like this:
```
...#..
...#..
.##...
```
Your task is to calculate the minimum and the maximum number of moves required to fill the first column of the board with blocks.
questions.input_format: array.array.char `field` — a non-empty rectangular matrix of characters representing a field.
questions.output_format: array.integer — array of two elements, where the first element is the minimum number of moves and the second one is the maximum number of moves required to fill the first column. It is guaranteed that the maximum number of moves doesn't exceed 12.
questions.constraints:
$1 \le field.length \le 12$
$1 \le field[0].length \le 12$
Maximum number of moves $\le 12$ (guaranteed).
Execution time limit: 0.5 s (C++); memory limit 1 GB.
questions.function_signature: C++: vector<int> solution(vector<vector<char>> field); Python: def solution(field)

examples.explanation: We need to choose the first row once and the third row three times.

To minimize the number of moves we need to choose the first row three times. To maximize this number, we need to choose the third row three times, then the second row twice, and the first row one time.

questions.explanation: Simulate a throw: walk right along the chosen row until the next cell is a block/edge, then drop down while the cell below is empty. A throw is only legal if the leftmost cell of the chosen row is empty. Run DFS/BFS over board states (encode as bitmasks, memoize) until column 0 is full; BFS depth gives the minimum, memoized DFS longest path gives the maximum. Depth <= 12 keeps the state space small.

questions.pattern: binary search on cooldown k with greedy cyclic schedule
questions.title: Maximum Cooldown k for Training Exercises
questions.statement:
In preparation for a sports tournament, you have $n$ training exercises available. Completing the $i$-th exercise improves your skills by `arr[i]` points. You can only perform one exercise per day, and once you complete an exercise, you must wait $k$ days before repeating it. For example, if $k=2$ and you perform exercise 1 on day 1, you cannot repeat it on days 2 and 3, but can do it again on day 4.

Given two targets: achieve at least $c$ skill points within $d$ days. Determine the maximum $k$ that allows you to meet this goal. If no such $k$ exists or $k$ is arbitrarily large, output $-1$.
questions.input_format: integer `n` — number of exercises; integer64 `c` — amount of skill points you have to gain at least within `d` days; integer `d` — number of days; array.integer `arr` — skill points gained on completing the i-th exercise.
questions.output_format: integer64 — the maximum k that allows you to gain at least c skill points within d days; if not possible or k is arbitrarily large, return -1.
questions.constraints:
$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$
$1 \le c \le 10^{16}$
$1 \le d \le 2 \cdot 10^5$
$1 \le arr[i] \le 10^9$
Execution time limit: 0.5 s (C++); memory limit 1 GB.

examples.explanation: With k=2: Day 1 do exercise 2 (+2), Day 2 do exercise 1 (+1), Day 3 do nothing, Day 4 do exercise 2 (+2). Total 2+1+2 = 5.

questions.explanation: Sort arr descending. For a fixed k the optimal plan cycles through the top min(n, k+1) exercises every k+1 days, so total(k) = full_cycles * prefix[min(n,k+1)] + prefix[min(n, rem)] with full_cycles = d / (k+1), rem = d % (k+1). total(k) is non-increasing in k, so binary search the largest k in [0, d] with total(k) >= c. If even k=0 fails -> -1; if k = d works (i.e. sum of top min(n,d) >= c) then k is arbitrarily large -> -1. O(n log n + log d).

questions.title: Rod Cutting for Maximum Revenue
questions.statement: Serling Enterprises buys long steel rods and cuts them into shorter rods, which it then sells. Each cut is free. Given a rod of length `n` and an array of prices `v`, where `v[i]` stands for the price of a piece with a length of `i`, determine the maximum revenue that you can obtain by cutting up the rod and selling the pieces.
questions.input_format: integer `n` — rod length; array.integer `v` — `v[i]` is the price of a piece of length `i` (v[0] = 0).

examples.explanation: A rod of length 4 costs 7. Cutting into 4 pieces of length 1 gives 8; 2 pieces of length 2 also gives 8; pieces of lengths 1 and 3 give 2 + 7 = 9, which is the maximum possible.

questions.explanation: dp[0] = 0; dp[L] = max over i in 1..L of v[i] + dp[L - i]. Answer dp[n]. O(n^2) time, O(n) space.
